d92fbfdbf6fc8fa5e40ec87884ddc9558eec1c0b.body:
The strip is the titlebar, but only a few pixels of it ever dragged.

Tauri reads a bare `data-tauri-drag-region` as *direct hits only* —
`el === composedPath[0]` in its injected script. The tab list is
`flex-1`, so its scroller covers the strip and is the target for every
press but the sliver of padding at the very edge. The attribute was
right when the tabs left gaps around themselves; once they filled the
strip there was nothing left to land on.

`deep` drags from anywhere in the subtree. It does not cost the tabs
their clicks: the same script refuses to drag when it passes a clickable
element on the way up, and a tab is a `role="tab"`, which is in its list.

Checked by running Tauri's own `isDragRegion` against real hit-tested
points: the middle of the strip, the space right of the tabs and the
padding all drag, and a press on a tab still does not.

6cdea19baa006828eac7e7417196e0239c86c4a2.body:
Clear lost its lit edge on every host, not just the one that needed it
to. WebKitGTK in a transparent window fills a positioned panel's layer
with opaque white around the rounded pill, so the clear surface gives up
its containing block — and the reveal, which is masked to that box, goes
with it. That repair was written unscoped, so macOS paid for a bug it
does not have.

It was in three places, which is why it looked total: the panel's class
list dropped `relative` and the border box, a CSS rule flattened the
panel to static, and the reveal itself carried `hidden`. All three now
ask the compositor, the way the transcript's WebKitGTK rules already do
— `layout` flattens, `layer` does not.

Clear is the surface with the most to lose here. It has no frame at all,
so the lit edge is the only thing that says where the window ends or
where it can be grabbed.

Verified in the browser preview, which is a layer compositor like macOS:
in clear the panel keeps `position: relative`, its 1px border box and its
18px radius, and the reveal spans the panel and lights under the pointer.

b05e7fa9bd2ebe6551003df3f675af2f98fe8476.body:
* shell: split chrome from the conversation strip

App was rendering the panel and owning the tab/turn rules at once.
The skills want a component that either renders or coordinates; the
strip's invariants (never empty, drafts per conversation, idle →
thinking → streaming) now live in conversation.ts so the chrome can
stay a view. Tests pin the stand-in behaviour; there is still no
agent runtime.

Co-authored-by: Saurav  <saurav.panthee@gmail.com>

* host: pin linux like macos and survive a missing tray

The panel frame and the tray were one module, so a Linux host with no
menu bar extra had nowhere to put placement, frost, or a missing-tray
fallback. panel.rs owns the frame; host.rs owns the seam; the webview
is pinned in GtkFixed the same way WKWebView is pinned, so a resize
does not jitter the composer. Tray creation, shortcuts, and frost are
survivable. Close quits when there is no tray. Hide-on-blur stays a
macOS extra behaviour.

Co-authored-by: Saurav  <saurav.panthee@gmail.com>

* host: keep linux clicks from aborting the panel

Tauri's undecorated resize handler unwraps webview.parent().parent() as
a GtkWindow on every button-press. Nesting GtkFixed inside tao's vbox
made that a GtkBox; the unwrap panicked, GTK cannot unwind, and the
process aborted. The Fixed now replaces the vbox so the grandparent
stays the window.

Also skip gtk_window_resize when the unrealized window reports height 0,
compile the conversation hook as TSX so Vite's production build can
parse the JSX, and record that this lockfile needs rustc 1.85+.

a181ec5ef57124c245ba510d67fd9c07fbd157b1.body:
Detaching the webview from the window broke the page's account of how big
the window is, and the panel drew itself the size of the whole stage:
full screen width, with the transcript's empty state centred off-window
and the composer stretched across the desktop.

Tauri reads a window's inner size off its view, and the view is the very
thing `viewport` stops resizing. So `innerSize()` answered 1512x900 — the
stage — agreeing exactly with `innerHeight`, with `outerSize()`, and with
nothing the reader could see. The window resize event carries the same
measurement, so neither the opening size nor any later one was right.

AppKit's content rect is the one description of the window left that a
fixed webview cannot falsify. The host reads it and sends it: once as it
places the panel, then on every resize, with a command for a page that
reloaded mid-session and has no event coming.

The page also refuses a size that is not a real length. Such a value is
written as an invalid custom property, which CSS resolves not to the
`100%` fallback but to `auto` — and an `auto` panel collapses to the
height of its composer, because the transcript's `flex-1` has nothing
definite left to divide.

06f49b3bdfca1b30687199304aa2d3c8761510ad.body:
Dragging the window's top edge moved the composer by up to 90pt, in a
sawtooth that reset each time the page caught up, on an edge macOS holds
exactly still.

The cause is two properties of `WKWebView`, both in `WebViewImpl.mm`: the
last frame the web process committed hangs off an internal *flipped*
subview, so it is positioned from the view's top left corner; and that
subview clips to its bounds, so a view that has already shrunk cuts off
whatever part of the older frame has not caught up. AppKit resizes the
view on every mouse event of the drag and the web process answers frames
later, so the corner moves and the pixels do not.

Together those rule out fixing it in the page — bottom-anchoring in CSS
lands at old height minus offset, and a counter-transform arrives in the
same commit as the relayout it was meant to correct — and they rule out
shrinking the view natively, since the clip then cuts the composer off
instead of moving it.

So the corner is not moved. The webview is sized once to the work area,
pinned to the window's bottom right, and left there; the window resizes
over the top of it. The page is told the window's size over the resize
events it already subscribes to and draws the panel that size against the
bottom right of the stage.

What is left is the dragged edge trailing by one relayout, under the
cursor, converging continuously rather than snapping at release.

99172e2c98f7a3a6b4643b7c8f49ba2d35f748d2.body:
The webview never sees a resize gesture. On a borderless resizable
NSWindow macOS claims the frame first, so the panel's own handle never
receives a pointerdown and the page is given no pointer events at all
until the drag ends. Every earlier attempt derived the pin from pointer
state and so pinned nothing; what stayed on screen was whatever opacity
was last written before the page went blind -- full strength if the
pointer settled on the edge, nothing if it clipped outside on the way
in, which is the whole of why the same handle appeared to work or fail
depending on where it was grabbed.

live_resize.rs observes NSWindowWillStartLiveResize and
DidEndLiveResize and forwards them, which is a true pin and a true
unpin, and which also distinguishes a drag from the tray's programmatic
re-fit. That deletes the quiet timer, the burst counter, the
arm-on-second-event guard, the pointer-release heuristic and its
backstop, along with the latent capture-phase blur bug they carried.

Underneath sat a second bug: --edge-x/y are frozen pixel offsets, and
the ring only spans the current box, so once the height shrank past
frozenY - 48 no lit pixel touched it. A top grab freezes y near 0 and
the top ring is at y=0 at every height, which is the asymmetry, with no
branch in the code. The point is now projected onto the edge captured
at resize-started -- the grabbed one -- rather than the nearest edge
each frame, which would hand the glow to a border nobody is dragging as
soon as the panel grew.

74f286c4ffff6d005281fcf47b6a1bc73682c2cf.body:
A native drag is run by the window server, which synthesises moves that
do not reliably carry button state. Inferring the end from
`event.buttons` cut the pin short mid-resize; the glow then fell back to
plain proximity, which still lights near where the drag began and dies
as soon as the pointer travels along the edge — exactly the reported
symptom.

Nothing in pointermove ends a drag now. mouseup, pointerup,
pointercancel and blur are all listened for and the first to arrive
releases the pin, since the release can land outside the webview and no
single one of those is guaranteed to reach the page.

onPointerMove cleared the drag flag on any move, so a single stray
event between pointerdown and the native drag's takeover cancelled it,

rest of the resize. Only a move with no button held ends a drag now.

While dragging, the glow pins to full rather than computing a distance:
the panel's edge is moving with the pointer, so the distance would
flicker. A window-level mouseup releases the pin, since the release can

192f0017545bcc3fd6c9ba9d2f5c3b073ae969f8.body:
A radial gradient in the Nessa rim spectrum, centred on the pointer and
masked down to the border ring by the same two-layer exclude the
PillComposer rim uses, so only the stretch of outline nearest the
pointer lights rather than the whole edge. Strength follows distance to
the nearest edge, so the border answers anywhere around the perimeter,
not only at the resize handle. Nothing animates on a loop: the gradient
moves because the pointer does.

Position and strength are written to the element from an animation
frame, never through state, so pointer movement cannot re-render the
conversation tree.

Also fixes the clear surface rendering as a filled panel: removing the
NSVisualEffectView left the window holding the opaque background that
effect was painted over, so the window is now put back to fully
transparent explicitly.

0af079f1774a286debc04e13f7d19d82d81b038f.body:
Mark the unlink-before-remove order as load-bearing: src-tauri/target is
a symlink into the shared cache, and a recursive delete that followed it
would wipe every worktree's compiled dependencies.

Add `worktree.sh clean` as the non-destructive counterpart to
`cargo clean`, which on a shared target throws away every worktree's
dependency builds.

96a0ae5fc41bde703b5aaa5171050f835bcba0e9.body:
Worktrees share the main checkout's src-tauri/target, so a new one
recompiles only this app's crate (~27s) rather than its ~500 dependency
crates. They are created as siblings because the design system is a
relative link: dependency that a nested path would not resolve.
